idiom_name: trait with a lazy val sttp backend and delegating methods
implementation_notes: A trait or final class holds the HTTP backend as a lazy val (sttp's SttpBackend) so the heavy client is constructed on first use, and exposes methods that build requests, send them and deserialize, translating Either/exception results into a domain error type; the lookup role is the configured base URI or a resolver invoked once per tenant. What replaces the classic structure: a trait plus its backend replaces the delegate/lookup/service class trio, and mixing in a test double replaces the stub delegate. Hand-write it when the delegate must aggregate calls or hide a generated stub's types.
code_sketch:
trait BillingApi {
  private lazy val backend = HttpClientSyncBackend()   // constructed once
  protected def baseUrl: String
  def createInvoice(cmd: CreateInvoice): Invoice =
    basicRequest
      .post(uri"$baseUrl/invoices")
      .body(cmd)
      .response(asJson[Invoice])
      .send(backend)
      .body match
        case Right(inv) => inv
        case Left(err)  => throw BillingUnavailable(err.toString)
}
pitfalls: The shared lazy val backend is thread-safe, but it must be closed on shutdown or non-daemon threads and connections leak.
asJson failures surface as sttp DeserializationException rather than a transport error - mapping both to one domain error hides which layer failed.
Trait initialization order: abstract defs used inside a constructor can observe null; keep the backend purely lazy and initialize nothing eagerly.
